sentences.text: Pelargopappus is an extinct genus of bird.
The genus was named by Stejneger in 1885, building on a species originally described by Milne-Edwards in 1868.
Today, only one species, P. magnus, is officially recognized.
It is an extinct raptor related to the secretarybird.
Researcher Cécile Mourer-Chauviré supported placing the genus in the family Sagittariidae and concluded that Amynoptilon is a synonym of Pelargopappus.
However, the Paleobiology Database lists the parent group as Accipitridae and classifies the genus within that family.
This bird lived in France during the early Miocene.
